rows.question: When customers asked for 'a mobile app' in the survey, which specific things did they say they wanted to do or have (alerts, offline access, speed, an icon on the home screen)?
Which web commitments (promised features, contract deliverables, maintenance) fall due in the next six months, and how many developer-weeks do they take?
Do customers who say 'mobile app' mean a separate downloadable app, or would a much better mobile site satisfy them?
rows.note: meaning of survey request; no hidden fact

rows.question: Could your three developers build the app with a cross-platform framework that reuses what they already know from the web product?
rows.note: asking about developers building cross-platform reveals none has shipped one

rows.question: What evidence do you have that the current mobile web experience is what keeps existing customers from using the product weekly?
rows.note: evidence about mobile web problems would cite the login drop-off

rows.question: Where does the statement that about half of your visitors are on mobile come from, and does it count existing customers, new visitors, or both?
rows.note: traffic source; session length not implied

rows.question: Of the customers who say they want an app, how many already use your mobile site every week?
rows.note: overlap of app requesters and mobile users; no hidden fact

rows.question: Among existing customers who open the product on a phone, at which screens or steps do they stall or leave?
rows.note: where users stall reveals 70% leave at login

rows.question: Would an installable web app (a PWA) with push notifications cover what the survey wants, at a fraction of the effort?
Is the six-month limit for the weekly active user goal fixed by someone outside the team, or could it move?
